# Build plan — the ticket board (Phase 5)

> **Status: drafted 2026-07-04; revised 2026-07-06; Phase 7 QA batch and rulings 2026-07-09–12 recorded in the rows and dated notes below (labelled channels T-089; the record turns inward T-104)** against the plan review and the surfaces-alignment rulings (grill tracker session record): M4 restructured to the Ask / Editor / Sandbox surface split, the Work item and wall-test subjects added to the seed, the append-only shape reconciled with Run/Step state transitions, the embeddings adapter corrected, T-021 split, and the build enablers T-083–T-085 added. The implementation plan: the walking skeleton broken into tickets with blocking relationships, plus the phased roadmap for everything after. This is the Phase 5 artefact of the [7-phases method](https://www.aihero.dev/my-7-phases-of-ai-development) — Phases 1–4 are the design layer (idea = overview, research = the Legora reference, PRD = the [walking skeleton](walking-skeleton.md) + [data model](data-model.md) + [contracts](contracts.md)). Phase 6 (execution) works this board; Phase 7 (QA) runs the end-to-end acceptance in the walking skeleton and raises new tickets here.
>
> **Scope discipline:** skeleton tickets are execution-ready; post-skeleton slices are a roadmap only, ticketed when their slice starts (matching the data model's drawer-by-drawer rule). The board lives in this file for now; export to GitHub Issues when we want agents working it in parallel.

## How to read a ticket

`T-###` — title. **Deps:** tickets that must be done first. **Done when:** the acceptance test, drawn from the walking skeleton's milestone acceptance. Package names from [repo-structure.md](repo-structure.md). A ticket is sized for one focused agent run (roughly a PR each).

**Definition of done, every ticket:** typed against `packages/contracts`; unit-tested; no surface reaches below the API; no code path resolves its own permissions (component 2 rule); lints and builds clean in CI.

---

## ⚠ One named build-time decision — skeleton auth

The design layer defers real identity/security to the infra/security session (component 1, open). The skeleton still needs a login. **Decision taken for the skeleton, to be superseded by that session:** email + password session login for the seeded users (`POST /auth/session`, httpOnly cookie), plus Entra ID SSO on the Copilot path (M6, where Microsoft mandates it). No self-serve signup, no password reset, no roles beyond what the data model already carries. This is scaffolding, not the security model; it is listed here so it is a recorded choice, not an accident.

**Production identity is committed as Entra-first (recorded 2026-07-04):** most users will arrive through Microsoft Entra (Azure AD), so production login is Entra ID SSO (OIDC) as the primary path, with the skeleton's password login retained only as a break-glass/dev mechanism to be decided at the infra/security session. The build already enables this: identity is established at one API boundary only (T-021/T-023, contracts principle 3), `User.external_identity` carries the Entra subject from Drawer 1, and T-071 exercises the full Entra → User → Participant mapping. Adding web SSO later is an additive login route, not a rework.

### Parallel tracks

Sequential spine: **T-001 → T-003/T-009 → migrations → T-020 → T-030 → T-041 → T-046 → T-082 → T-053 → T-080.** Off the spine, these run concurrently: T-010 (model), T-002 (CI), T-083 (config/bootstrap) and T-049 (UI tokens from the mockups) from day one; T-050/T-051 (scaffold + sandbox surface) once contracts and the skeleton auth exist (T-009/T-021 — shell work can begin earlier against a stubbed session), well before M3 completes; T-084 (e2e harness) beside M4; T-085 then T-070 (Copilot enablers + manifest) once T-046 is stable; T-012 (ingestion) beside M1.

**UI track:** the visual spec lives in [docs/design/mockups/](../design/mockups-legacy/index.html) — eight Legora-clean screens (third cut, 2026-07-06: workspace landing, project home, Ask chat, Editor with chat + suggestion panel, foldered library, sandbox, review, owner run-audit), restructured to the owner's wireframes and the surfaces-alignment rulings (grill tracker session record), benchmarked on the observed Legora UI review ([docs/reference/legora-ui-review.md](../reference/legora-ui-review.md)). The project nav is Home · Ask · Editor · Documents · Review · Sandbox · Tools · History (Workflows renamed Tools, T-109; History added, T-108); Knowledge is staged with the moat slices (component 8 §6). The alignment session is closed (all items ruled 2026-07-06 — grill tracker session record). ## Slice A — Document management: the controlled lifecycle *(ticketed 2026-07-18)*

> **Status: ✅ built, T-113–T-129 all landed 2026-07-18** (one autonomous session; every ticket its own verified commit, CI green throughout). The T-129 acceptance suite drives the whole journey: plan → consolidate/confirm → draft → freeze → org-private internal QA → promote the QA-accepted frozen version → rounds/comments/codes → issue → respond → v2 → accept → library + grounding; plus the rejected pathway and the wall negatives. **Honest deviations & follow-ups:** review reads happen against the frozen version's text with the PDF rendition downloadable — the in-PDF anchored viewer (pdf.js) is the noted follow-up; the internal cycle launches when the freeze container carries a confirmed lead reviewer (no separate launch endpoint); drawer-5 comments landed as the `review_comments` table (clearer beside `sandbox_comments`); T-123/T-124/T-126's API halves shipped in one commit and their surfaces in T-127's cycle page; transmittal "notifies recipients" is a recorded fact, not delivery (the parked notification model); post-acceptance promotion opens a new revision cycle (pinned in tests); office→PDF conversion for uploads waits on the infra converter.

*Design session closed 2026-07-18 → ADRs 0032 (two-scope role-agnostic cycle), 0033 (per-org plans, appointment grants, administration), 0034 (canonical format, renditions); the data model's Drawers 1/2/3/5 are the table spec. Mockups for the new surfaces (plan builder, DRR table, PDF review) are drawn per-ticket as each surface starts, benchmarked on the ProjectWise friction map (docs/reference) — "no wizard" is the standing acceptance test for promote and freeze. The T-112 participants endpoint widens to the project roster per ADR-0033 (in T-117).*

## Slice A2 — Producing-side surfaces: the TIDP page, the sandbox drawer, bind & the multiplayer thread (prototype) *(ticketed 2026-07-23)*

> **Status: ✅ built, T-145–T-162 all landed 2026-07-23** (one session; each ticket its own verified commit — typecheck 13/13, db 21, api 116, governance 34, contracts 5, orchestration 13, e2e 33 green throughout). The producing-side deliverable lifecycle as **interactive surfaces** — turning the Slice A mechanical spine (T-113–T-129) and the ADR-0035 acknowledgement gate (T-134–T-138) into a browser-drivable prototype a consultant can actually walk. **One full-lifecycle slice** (owner-chosen 2026-07-23): TIDP page + schema → sandbox drawer + folders → create/bind documents → collaborate (shared thread + attached-source working set) → launch internal review from the folder view → freeze → promote → transmittal → acknowledgement. Multiplayer ships as **shared-thread visibility now, real-time presence/sync deferred** (owner-chosen). "No wizard" held for bind, freeze and promote. **Honest deviations & follow-ups:** `sandbox_documents.sandbox_id` stays nullable (the create path sets it, but the old implicit-org path remains) — NOT NULL when every write is wired; the sandbox drawer shows all the org's documents (filtered to a sandbox when one is selected); the T-162 acceptance stops at bind (promote-to-accept is the Slice A path, T-129); an owner→org transmittal/acknowledgement is exercised at the API level (T-137/T-161), the e2e drives the producing-side chain; real-time multiplayer presence deferred; super-user tier still T-133.

Mostly a surfaces slice on existing mechanics; new backend only where session B added it. Mockups drawn per-ticket, benchmarked on the ProjectWise friction map and SharePoint for the sandbox drawer.*

## The roadmap after the skeleton (coarse — ticketed when its slice starts)

Ordered by the wedge-first logic of the overview; each slice names its design gate from the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md). Nothing here is execution-ready by design.

**Slice A — Document management: the controlled lifecycle** — ✅ **designed (ADRs 0032/0033/0034, 2026-07-18) and ticketed: T-113–T-129 above.** The review-cycle entry surface was already mocked ([review.html](../design/mockups-legacy/review.html)); the DRR table, PDF viewer and plan-builder mockups are drawn per-ticket as each surface starts.

**Slice A2 — Producing-side surfaces (prototype)** — ✅ **designed (ADRs 0036/0038/0039 + refinements to 0022/0032, 2026-07-22) and ticketed: T-145–T-162 above.** The producing-side lifecycle as interactive surfaces on the Slice A spine: the standalone TIDP page + schema/code-builder, the SharePoint-shaped sandbox drawer with folder-view actions, the bind action, the attached-source working set, and the multiplayer shared thread (visibility now, real-time deferred). One full-lifecycle slice; mockups per-ticket.

**Slice A2.1 — Real interfaces (the producing-side UI, done properly)** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-163–T-167).** Slice A2 proved the mechanics but shipped substandard UI: `window.prompt()` browser dialogs, emoji-as-icons, a nonexistent `.input` CSS class, no real TIDP builder, no metadata editors, and bound documents you couldn't see or navigate. This slice replaces that with best-in-class interfaces grounded in the design system (design-rules.md §A–§G), the ProjectWise/AssetWise friction map (file/metadata separation kept; "No Wizard", auto-surfaced attributes, safe basic ops — B1/B3/B4), and the Legora + ISO-19650-CDE register pattern (an editable deliverable register, a detail/metadata side-panel, searchable combobox pickers). **No `window.prompt`, no emoji-icons, elevation-4 modals, semantic tokens only** are the standing acceptance tests.

- **T-163 — UI foundation: Modal + form controls.** A `Modal` primitive (elevation-4 overlay, focus-trap, ESC/backdrop close, header/body/footer) and form controls (`Field`, `TextInput`, `TextArea`, `SelectInput`, `Combobox` searchable picker) in `@infora/ui` with CSS from the tokens and a component test. Retires `window.prompt` and the phantom `.input` class.
- **T-164 — The deliverable register (TIDP builder).** The Plan page becomes an editable register grid; "New deliverable" opens a proper modal form — the code-builder as live field dropdowns composing a preview reference, plus title/discipline/authoring metadata — "No Wizard". A row opens a detail panel.
- **T-165 — The bind dialog + bound-document visibility.** A modal with a **searchable combobox of the org's accessible unbound TIDP rows** (code + title) replaces the prompt; bound documents show their code and link to the deliverable, and the register shows each row's bound draft.
- **T-166 — Metadata editors (library + sandbox).** A metadata detail panel: container identity (read-only) + authoring metadata (editable, container PATCH); sandbox-document authoring metadata editable via an extended sandbox PATCH — grouped fields, real controls (file/metadata separation, B4 auto-surfaced attributes).
- **T-167 — Replace remaining prompts + emoji-icons; verify.** Convert the other prompt sites (sandbox create, folder, scope grant, working-set pin, transmit, acknowledge) to modals/forms; swap emoji glyphs for Lucide; update the e2e; full verification.

**Slice A2.2 — Hardening & follow-through** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-168–T-175).** Closes the gaps flagged after A2.1: accessibility of the new primitives, lint hygiene, dark mode, the deferred deviations, and the two bigger deferred items (the elevated tier, real-time presence).
- **T-168 — Primitive accessibility (design-rules §D).** `Combobox` gets keyboard navigation (↑/↓/Enter/Escape) and `aria` roles; `Modal` gets a real focus-trap and focus-restore on close.
- **T-169 — Lint clean.** Run `pnpm check` (deps + lint + typecheck + tests) and clear anything it flags on the Slice A2/A2.1 code.
- **T-170 — Dark-mode pass.** Render the new modals/forms/register/sandbox in dark and fix any token gaps (design-rules §G item 1).
- **T-171 — `sandbox_documents.sandbox_id` → NOT NULL.** Backfill any nulls, make the create paths always set it, tighten the column.
- **T-172 — Humanise status labels.** A shared work-item-status label map (`in_production` → "In production") used by the register, sandbox and work-item surfaces.
- **T-173 — Register row detail panel.** A slide-over showing a deliverable's dates, reviewers and authoring team beside its metadata.
- **T-174 — The elevated (super-user) tier (T-133 realised).** A server-side gate for destructive lifecycle actions (close-reject, supersede, withdraw), surfaced only to elevated participants; reconciled with the org admin (ADR-0033) and ADR-0016's owner/member collapse.
- **T-175 — Real-time multiplayer presence (first cut).** A presence layer — who is viewing/editing a document — as the first concrete step of ADR-0039's deferred real-time half (heartbeat + read; live avatars in the editor), short of a full CRDT sync engine.

**Slice A2.3 — Classes of user + plan/scheme polish** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-176–T-178)**, from owner feedback. Turns T-174's flat `elevated` flag into named **classes of user** and gates the plan/scheme surfaces on them. Design captured in [grill-sessions/prompt-user-classes.md](../grill-sessions/prompt-user-classes.md).
- **T-176 — Classes of user (capability matrix).** Derive the class from `(membershipRole × elevated)` — **owner super-user** / **guest super-user** / **ordinary** — no new stored role (doesn't reopen ADR-0016). Governance capability predicates (`canEditPlan`, `canEditScheme`, `canProposeScheme`); gate the plan create/patch API on super-user (editing the TIDP now requires it), the scheme PUT on owner-super, propose on guest-super; expose the class to the UI via /me.
- **T-177 — Clear "Edit coding scheme" button + role-aware surfaces.** Replace the hidden link with a prominent button; the schema page is fully editable by the owner super-user, propose-only for the guest super-user, view-only otherwise; the plan hides "New deliverable"/metadata-edit from non-super-users.
- **T-178 — Remove the redundant discipline free-text.** The New-deliverable modal keeps the scheme's discipline **dropdown** (when present) and drops the standalone "Discipline (optional)" free-text box.

**Slice A2.4 — Sandbox structure, freeze & versioning** — 🔨 **in build 2026-07-25**, from owner feedback on the sandbox surface. Prompt in [grill-sessions/prompt-sandbox-structure.md](../grill-sessions/prompt-sandbox-structure.md).
- **T-179 — Sandbox folder-tree UI (SharePoint-shaped).** The flat sandbox table becomes a nested folder tree: folders nest and documents live *inside* their folder, with expand/collapse, a current-folder breadcrumb, and re-filing by drag-and-drop **or** the keyboard-accessible Move dialog (the `/folders/:id/move` + `/sandbox-documents/:id/move` endpoints already existed, T-153; a move never changes access, only where a document sits — ADR-0036). Fixed a latent gap: the vite dev proxy didn't forward `/sandboxes`, `/folders`, or `/sandbox-scope-grants`, so the browser's folder calls hit the SPA fallback — the first e2e (sandbox-tree.spec) to exercise them surfaced it. `Button` gained an `aria-label`/`title` passthrough so per-row "Move" buttons carry their row's context for a screen reader. *(Honest deviation: drag-and-drop is the mouse enhancement, verified by code + render; the Move dialog is the tested/accessible path — native HTML5 DnD is unreliable to drive in Playwright.)*
- **T-181 — Per-sandbox super-user settings + the folder-creation toggle (ADR-0040).** Settings live on the sandbox row (first setting: `allow_member_folder_create`, default on). Configuration is a super-user act split along the wall — a guest super-user configures a sandbox its own org owns, the owner-super configures any (`canConfigureSandbox`); an ordinary participant never configures. With the toggle off, only a super-user of the sandbox may add folders; ordinary members work within the laid-out structure. `PATCH /sandboxes/:id/settings`; the read carries `allowMemberFolderCreate` + a per-requester `canConfigure` self fact; a Settings modal + gated "New folder" on the surface. No new stored role (composes from `elevated` + `owningOrganisationId`). Migration `0027_sandbox-settings`.
- **T-182 — Create-folder-structure builder (ADR-0040).** A super-user lays out a whole nested tree at once instead of one folder at a time: an indented-outline builder (two spaces / a tab per level) with a live preview, creating the structure in one `POST /sandboxes/:id/folder-structure` (super-user-gated, `canConfigureSandbox`; ≤200 folders). Reusable folder templates (project-/org-level starter structures) are a deliberate **follow-up** — the free-form builder lands first.
- **T-180 — Freeze is a real check-out (ADR-0032 addendum).** The Slice-A honest deviation left Freeze inert (it only locked the head when an internal round opened). Now **every freeze locks the head** — standalone check-out and review-round check-out are one `head_locked` mechanism, two triggers; a plain check-out upgrades to a formal round by freezing again with a lead reviewer, and a redundant plain re-freeze is refused. The lock is on the document, so it is **format-agnostic**: it refuses the manual PATCH, an ambient-history restore, an uploaded-file→text conversion, and soft-delete; the editor canvas goes read-only. **Release** ("check in") is audited both ways on an append-only `sandbox_checkout_events` trail, by the checkout author, the freeze series' lead reviewer, or an elevated super-user — not while an internal round is open (the round's issue/close is the release). New `POST /sandbox-documents/:id/release`; migration `0026_sandbox-checkout-events`.

- **T-187 — New-sandbox wizard: private/shared → organisations → people (ADR-0042, owner feedback).** The single-scope modal becomes a short wizard: step 1 name + Private (my org) / Shared (across orgs, owner-super only); step 2 (shared) pick the organisations; step 3 who has access — everyone in those orgs, or specific people (a checkbox picker). The super-user admits participants **at creation** rather than only afterward. `POST /sandboxes` accepts `organisationIds` / `participantIds` (validated on-project, de-duped, owning-org/creator skipped) and creates the grants alongside the auto-grant.
- **T-186 — Sandbox provisioning is a super-user act + personal sandboxes (ADR-0042, owner feedback).** Creating a sandbox is now super-user-only (`canCreateSandbox`): an ordinary member cannot; a guest-super creates private (own-org) sandboxes; a shared (cross-org) sandbox stays the owner-super's act (ADR-0018). Every participant gets an **auto-provisioned personal sandbox** (named-user, granted to just them, server-created, one per participant via a partial unique index) — created lazily on first sandbox read. The surface hides the create control from non-super-users, labels the personal card and sorts it first. Ordinary members see their personal sandbox + any they're a member of, and create folders (not sandboxes) within. Migration `0028_sandbox-personal`. *(Flagged inference: guest-super confined to private creation — relax the `multi_org` branch if the owner wants any super-user to open shared, but that moves cross-org visibility off the owner.)*
- **T-185 — Folder-structure builder: interactive tree, no whitespace (owner feedback).** The indented-outline textarea (T-182) relied on the user managing two-space/tab indentation, which was fiddly and misparsed. Replaced with an interactive builder: a name field per folder, a **subfolder** button to nest one inside, Enter to add the next folder at the same level, and per-row remove — nesting shown by visual indentation, no whitespace to manage. The API (nested node spec) is unchanged.
- **T-184 — Sandbox selector as informative cards (owner feedback).** The flat chip list becomes a grid of cards, one per sandbox: name, the owning organisation, and whether it is **private** (single-org/team/named-user) or **shared** (multi-org) — a shared card also lists the other organisations in scope. Clicking a card selects it and reveals its folder tree below (unchanged). The list read gains `organisationIdsInScope` (the live org-grants) for the owner/shared display; names resolve client-side from the roster.
- **T-183 — Sandbox version numbering + the ISO 19650 P/C scheme (ADR-0041).** One working series in the sandbox (`v0.1, 0.2, …`, the ambient history; a plain check-out freezes the current working revision under its `v0.x`); `P{NN}` on the first formal issue or promotion (freeze-that-opens-a-round, or promotion — each client round a further P); `C{NN}` the contractual revision issued on client acceptance (a new immutable current Version of the accepted content, since `version_reference` is immutable — retrieval/library/plan/renditions key on `is_current`). The sandbox read carries a `workingRevision` and the ambient history a `v0.x` per snapshot; the sandbox surface shows the working revision on each document row. Updated the freeze (`P{n}`→`v0.x`/`P{NN}`) and promotion (`v{n}`→`P{NN}`) reference generation.

**Slice A2.5 — The TIDP wizard** — 🔨 **in build 2026-07-25**, from owner feedback. A super-user defines the full deliverable-plan (TIDP) schema, and producing orgs edit their TIDP against it. Owner rulings: **unify** the schema (code fields flagged as segments), **reuse** the appointment tables + add a document-owner, **reuse** `withdrawn` + a reason for removal.
- **T-188 — Unified deliverable schema + default + owner editor.** The coding scheme becomes one unified TIDP schema: each field carries a `type` (text/select/date/person/people/serial), `required`, an `inCode` flag (composes the coded reference) and/or a `role` slot (author/document owner/reviewer/lead reviewer). The code-builder composes from the `inCode` fields (backward-compatible: legacy fields default to code). A **default Infora schema** (ISO-19650-shaped: seven code segments + purpose/suitability/format metadata + the four role slots) preloads when none is saved and is fully editable by the owner-super (change fields, add fields, reorder, reset-to-default). Rebuilt the schema editor around the unified fields.
- **T-189 — TIDP editing (guest-super).** The New-deliverable modal is schema-driven: the code fields build the reference and the schema's metadata fields (purpose/suitability/format…) render as a Details form (required-gated). The deliverable detail drawer gains a **document owner** picker (a single participant of the producing org, informational, amendable — `PATCH /containers/:id/document-owner`) and a **Remove from plan…** action that keeps the container as a record (`state → withdrawn` + free-text reason via `POST …/withdrawal`) with a **Restore** (`…/restoration`). Producing-org super-user only; migration `0029_deliverable-owner-withdrawal`.

**Slice B — The Word add-in** *(design settled, component 8).* The consultant authoring surface: tracked-changes suggestions with citation + rationale, accept/edit/reject as Signals, central M365 deployment. Needs Slice A's promotion path to be fully useful, but drafting on sandbox documents can land earlier.

**Slice C — Governance depth** *(part open: threshold tuning, retention/export — bucket A).* Rails as scoped records with the ADR-0030 intersection engine, grounding-threshold calibration, withheld-output UX, audit retention/export, user-UI-action audit sense.

**Slice D — Retrieval maturity** *(gate: Session 6 finish).* Contextual retrieval ("x in the context of y"), real channel ranking and budget, org-vs-programme precedence, per-viewer citation rendering — behind the unchanged ADR-0029 signature.

**Slice E — The moat loop** *(gate: Sessions 4, 5, 7 — must-grill, the cross-org confidentiality forks).* Org/programme context stores and drawers, the distillation engine with the ADR-0026 destination rule, precedent selection, the Signal sink, guidance notes (ADR pending), and the ADR-0026 within-tenant/cross-tenant training reconciliation flagged in the tracker.

**Slice F — Build-your-own** *(gate: Engine §5 opens — builder interface, tightening validation, sharing).* Custom tools (the Tools surface, T-109) and org-built agents: authoring through the builder in Tools, org-context storage, deploy-time rails inheritance, pre-deploy validation. The tool-scoping ruling (2026-07-13) and the wall-clean-definition stress test are on the tracker's builder theme.

**Slice G — Breadth surfaces** *(bucket A, reference-decidable).* Workspace home vs project home layout, the owner/client portfolio "control tower", programme views, mobile scope.

**Slice H — Connectors** *(deferred until the wedge is proven).* Integrate-configuration handover to an incumbent DMS; spatial/CAD/BIM by reference.

**Gate before any external pilot — the infra/security decision session** *(bucket C, component 1).* Cloud provider, blob/object storage for renditions, hosting and deployment, encryption and key management, tenant isolation, residency, production identity (replacing the skeleton auth above). The skeleton deliberately runs on the dev substrate until this is held.
